departments.name: 3D Modeling
departments.mission: Model every three-dimensional object the game needs, built to the project's triangle, texel and material budgets.

deliverables.name: Model List and Budgets
acceptance: Every required model listed with owner, priority and triangle budget
LOD and collision requirements stated per model class
Reuse plan showing which models can be instanced or reskinned

deliverables.name: Model Pack
acceptance: Every model is within its triangle budget and has correct scale and pivot
UVs are packed, normals correct and materials named to convention
Each model has LODs and a collision proxy where the budget requires it

deliverables.name: Topology and Budget Review
acceptance: Measured triangle and draw-call counts attached per model
Non-manifold geometry, inverted normals and missing UVs listed as zero
Every model imports cleanly into the project pipeline

gates: A model over its stated triangle budget is rejected unless the budget is revised
Missing LOD or collision proxy on a budgeted model is rejected

departments.name: 2D Art and Illustration
departments.mission: Produce all two-dimensional art: sprites, tiles, icons, illustrations and the 2D environments of the game.

deliverables.name: 2D Style Sheet
acceptance: Canvas sizes, pixel density and palette limits stated
Silhouette, outline and shading rules shown on sample assets
Animation frame counts and frame timing per state

deliverables.name: Sprite and Tileset Atlas
acceptance: Every sprite exists at the specified size with transparent background
Atlas packing plan keeps draw calls within the rendering budget
Animation frames are named and ordered to the state machine

deliverables.name: 2D Art Review
acceptance: No missing, misaligned or duplicate frames in the build
Palette and outline consistency verified across all sets

gates: A sprite outside its palette or canvas rule is rejected
Animation with missing frames is rejected

departments.name: Environment Art
departments.mission: Build the places: terrain, landscapes, cities, interiors and destructible environments that carry the world design into the build.

deliverables.name: Environment Plan
acceptance: Every area mapped to an art kit and a prop budget
Density, vista and landmark placement rules stated per biome
Interior and exterior transition rules defined

deliverables.name: Environment Kit and Dressed Areas
acceptance: Kit pieces snap to a stated grid and share one material set
Each dressed area meets its prop and draw-call budget
Collision and navmesh coverage present for every playable surface

deliverables.name: Environment Performance Review
acceptance: Measured draw calls, triangles and texture memory attached per area
Culling, LOD and occlusion verified in a profiled build
Any area over budget listed with a concrete fix

gates: An area without collision or navmesh coverage is rejected
An area over its prop budget without a listed fix is rejected

departments.name: Materials and Textures
departments.mission: Author the surface language of the game: PBR materials, texture sets and terrain layers that read correctly under every lighting condition.
capabilities: albedo, normal, roughness, metallic and height maps
texel density and texture budget management

deliverables.name: Material Library
acceptance: Each material lists its maps, resolution, texel density and licence
Seamless tiling verified on a test plane
Every material parameter exposed to the shader is documented

deliverables.name: Texture Budget and Compression Plan
acceptance: Texture memory measured per platform profile
Compression format chosen per map type with rationale
Any texture over budget has a downscale or atlas plan

gates: A material without a licence record is rejected
Non-power-of-two textures on mobile profiles are rejected unless justified

departments.name: Character Art
departments.mission: Create the people and creatures players look at for hundreds of hours: proportions, faces, clothing, armour and variation.

deliverables.name: Character Specification
acceptance: Every character class has a silhouette, palette and material plan
Customisation dimensions and their allowed values listed
Polygon, texture and bone budgets stated per class

deliverables.name: Character Pack
acceptance: Every character rigs and deforms correctly at the stated bone count
Skinning weights verified on extreme poses
Modular pieces share a material set and attach without gaps

deliverables.name: Character Review
acceptance: No visible seams, clipping or untextured areas in the build
All customisation combinations render without missing assets

inputs: character spec from D02 and D04
gates: A character without a rig and skinning test is rejected
Untextured or default-material areas in the build are rejected

departments.name: Animation
departments.mission: Make movement read: locomotion, combat, interaction, vehicles, creatures and procedural motion that feels responsive.
capabilities: combat, hit reaction and death animations

deliverables.name: Animation List and State Machine
acceptance: Every required animation listed with frame count, loop flag and root motion
State machine transitions and blend times specified in milliseconds
Cancel windows and input buffering rules stated per action

deliverables.name: Animation Set
acceptance: Every animation in the list exists and loops or ends cleanly
Root motion matches the movement speeds in the GDD
Foot sliding measured and within the stated tolerance

deliverables.name: Animation Review
acceptance: No missing, popping or T-posed states during a scripted playthrough
Hit reactions and death transitions verified on every rig class

inputs: combat design from D23 or D18
gates: An animation set that T-poses or pops in a build is rejected
Root motion inconsistent with GDD speeds is rejected

departments.name: Lighting and Rendering
departments.mission: Light the world believably and render it affordably: shadows, ambient terms, reflections, atmosphere and day/night cycles.
capabilities: ambient occlusion and indirect light approximation

deliverables.name: Lighting Plan
acceptance: Key, fill and rim intent defined per time of day and biome
Shadow strategy and cascade distances stated with numbers
Post-processing stack listed with cost estimates

deliverables.name: Lighting and Post Setup
acceptance: Lightmaps or probes baked and stored with the scene
Day/night interpolation verified across a full cycle
Every lighting feature has a documented quality tier

deliverables.name: Lighting Performance Review
acceptance: Frame cost of lighting and post measured per quality tier
Shadow and probe memory measured against the profile budget
Lowest tier verified playable on the weakest declared device

gates: A lighting feature with no quality tier or measured cost is rejected
Shadow bias artefacts visible in the build are rejected

departments.name: VFX
departments.mission: Deliver feedback with weight: impacts, explosions, smoke, fire, water, weather, destruction and magic effects within a particle budget.

deliverables.name: VFX List and Budget
acceptance: Every gameplay event mapped to an effect with priority
Particle and overdraw budgets stated per effect class
Cue timing in milliseconds aligned to animation cancel windows

deliverables.name: VFX Set
acceptance: Every listed effect exists, triggers on its event and cleans up
Effects pooled and capped to the stated particle budget
Effect LOD present for the lowest quality tier

deliverables.name: VFX Budget Review
acceptance: Worst-case simultaneous effects measured and within budget
Overdraw hotspots identified with a fix
Effects verified at the lowest quality tier

gates: An effect with no pooling or no cap is rejected
Visible overdraw spikes without a listed fix are rejected

departments.name: Sound Design
departments.mission: Give every action, surface and place a voice, and mix it so the player hears what matters.

deliverables.name: Sound Map
acceptance: Every audible event mapped to a sound with priority
Spatialisation, attenuation and concurrency rules stated
Licence or authorship recorded for every external sound

deliverables.name: Sound Set and Mix
acceptance: Every mapped event has at least one sound with variation
Loudness normalised to the project target and clipping-free
Compression and streaming format chosen per sound class

deliverables.name: Mix Review
acceptance: Combat, dialogue and ambience audible in a full scene without masking
Voice-count and memory measured against budget

gates: A sound without licence or authorship record is rejected
Clipping or unnormalised loudness in the mix is rejected

departments.name: Music Production
departments.mission: Compose a score that carries the game's identity and responds to what the player is doing.

deliverables.name: Music Direction
acceptance: Instrumentation, tempo and mood defined per game state
Motifs and their transformations described
Runtime and licensing constraints stated

deliverables.name: Soundtrack and Stems
acceptance: Every required state has music with seamless loop points
Stems delivered for adaptive mixing
Authorship and licence recorded for every track

deliverables.name: Adaptive Music Review
acceptance: Transitions between states verified without clicks or gaps
Music memory and streaming measured against budget

gates: A track without authorship and licence is rejected
A loop with an audible gap is rejected

departments.name: Cinematics
departments.mission: Direct and produce the game's scripted sequences: camera, staging, transitions and in-game storytelling.

deliverables.name: Cinematic Plan
acceptance: Every sequence listed with duration, trigger and skip behaviour
Shot list with framing and camera path
Subtitles, localisation and accessibility requirements stated

deliverables.name: Cutscene Set
acceptance: Every sequence plays in-engine without missing actors or audio
Skip, pause and subtitle controls all work
Camera does not clip through geometry in any shot

deliverables.name: Cinematic Review
acceptance: Frame pacing and audio sync verified in a built version
Every sequence tested at the lowest quality tier

inputs: music and sound from D14 and D15
gates: A sequence that cannot be skipped is rejected
Missing subtitles on spoken dialogue is rejected
